questions.question: Define position, velocity, and acceleration in kinematics.
questions.solution:
**Position:** Location of a particle relative to a reference frame (coordinate x, y, z).
**Velocity:** Rate of change of position with time â€” v = dx/dt; SI unit m/s.
**Acceleration:** Rate of change of velocity with time â€” a = dv/dt; SI unit m/sÂ².
questions.knowledgeNote: All three are vectors. Velocity is the first derivative of position; acceleration is the second derivative.
questions.answer: **Position:** the location of a body relative to a chosen origin and reference direction — specified by coordinates (x, or r as a position vector); it is where the body *is*. **Velocity:** the **rate of change of position** — v = dx/dt (or dr/dt) — a vector giving both speed and direction of motion; the magnitude of velocity is the speed. **Acceleration:** the **rate of change of velocity** — a = dv/dt — a vector; it is nonzero whenever the speed *or* the direction of motion changes (which is why uniform circular motion has acceleration). **Deep point:** the three quantities form a derivative chain — position, its first derivative (velocity), its second derivative (acceleration) — and each is a vector in 2-D/3-D motion.
